chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who performed the ritual bath for his Ihram, then clipped his nails, he said: He should wipe them with the water, and he does not repeat the bath.

key_terms.لإحرامه: for his Ihram (state of consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one clips their nails after performing Ghusl for Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies a practical nuance in the jurisprudence of Ihram, ruling that clipping nails after the ritual bath does not invalidate the purity established by the Ghusl. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between major ritual impurity (Junub) and minor impurities, ensuring that minor acts like nail trimming do not necessitate the heavier burden of repeating the full ritual bath.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
regarding a man who washes for his Ihraam, then clips his nails. Heasws said: ‘He should wipe them with the water, and he would not repeat the washing’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from certain persons of his people

who has said the following: “About a man who takes Ghusl (bath) for Ihram then trims his fingernails, abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘He should wipe them with water and he is not required to take Ghusl (bath) again.’”
